name: Drowned Sacellum
summary: At Blackfathom Deeps' entrance, the Drowned Sacellum lies submerged beneath the coast. Brackish saltwater and cavern roots surround its broken stones, now occupied by murlocs and makrura.

sections.title: A Submerged Sanctuary
sections.body: You enter the Drowned Sacellum just beyond Blackfathom Deeps' threshold. The chapel once offered quiet worship to Elune, but it has long since collapsed into the sea-swept abyss beneath Ashenvale's coast. Brackish pools swallow its ancient marble flagstones, where starfish cling beneath the cavern ceiling's massive roots. Dark wisps flicker dimly through the gloom, lighting a broken stone path. Careful steps along it lead deeper into the temple complex, toward the Pool of Ask'ar.

sections.title: Den of Scavengers
sections.body: Night elf caretakers left the Drowned Sacellum long ago, and shoreline scavengers now hold the ruins. Packs of aggressive murlocs and heavily armored makrura share the murky waters and attack anyone who disturbs their nesting grounds. Darker cultic threats lie deeper in the temple, but these predators guard the first stretch of the underground ruins.

faq.q: What was the Drowned Sacellum originally used for?
faq.answer: A sacellum is a small roofless shrine or chapel. Before the Sundering, this one served as an elven place of worship to Elune within the greater subterranean temple complex.

faq.q: What creatures inhabit this part of the caverns?
faq.answer: Wild murlocs and makrura occupy the flooded ruins. They thrive in the brackish pools and nesting crevices.

faq.q: How do you navigate past the Drowned Sacellum?
aliases: how to get through drowned sacellum
faq.answer: Carefully cross the crumbling, half-submerged platforms and pillars rising out of the water to reach the tunnel ahead, which leads to the Pool of Ask'ar.

faq.q: Where does the light in the cavern come from?
faq.answer: Dark wisps floating among thick, twisted tree roots that pierce the ceiling from the Ashenvale forests above provide the cavern's faint, eerie light.

angles.text: For a night elf, this ancient shrine's submersion in saltwater and its occupation by murlocs recall the Kaldorei heritage lost beneath the Zoram Strand.
As a druid, you can see massive tree roots piercing the stone ceiling from the surface above, proof that nature endures amid the corrupted underground waters.
